notes:
SHAPE 1, THE DESTINATION SPLIT. One wiki page, two client ids. My front matter says branch = 'the San d'Oria destination', so this record is the route that leaves Bastok for SAN D'ORIA first -- the page's '## After the walkthrough: Option 1: San d'Oria Path' -- and mission/bastok/9 is the same page's 'Option 2: Windurst Path'. The split point is bullet [2] of the shared '## Walkthrough': President Karst hands you the [KI] Letter to the consuls and asks you to 'head to either San d'Oria or Windurst'. Everything up to and including that bullet is common to both records (my step 1), which is why the two records are identical at rung 1 and share nothing after it. That is not sibling-importing: both halves are on THIS page, at this revision.

WHICH BULLETS BELONG TO THE OTHER RECORD. All thirteen bullets of 'Option 2: Windurst Path' are mission/bastok/9's, and none of them are here: Melek first, Kupipi for the [KI] Sword offering, Gold Skull for the [KI] Dull sword, Uu Zhoumo in Giddeus, Eyy Mon the Ironbreaker for the Aspir Knife, the Horlais Peak BCNM against the Dread Dragon, and the [KI] Kindred crest / [KI] Kindred report. I split where the page splits -- at its own two 'Option' headings -- because the routes share no content after Karst and a merged ladder would send half the players to the wrong battlefield.

BULLET NUMBERING. Steps 2-12 come from the 'Option 1: San d'Oria Path' After-section, whose bullets restart at [1]; that section carries two '==' sub-headings ('Bastok to San d'Oria', 'San d'Oria to Windurst') but the numbering runs continuously [1]..[9] across them, so a source_bullets value of 5 here means Option 1's [5], not the shared walkthrough's. Step 1 alone cites the shared '## Walkthrough' [1] and [2].

GIVER. The header's Start is the ROLE string 'Any Bastok Gate Guard' -- no NPC of that name exists and normalize_npc drops anything beginning 'Any ' as generic, so a literal copy would cost this mission its marker outright. The rendered '## Giver' block names all four Bastok gate guards from Category:Gate Guard, and any one of them opens the mission, so start.npc is the four-way multi-option string that build_index splits on ' or ' into one marker key each. start.zone and start.grid are null on purpose: the four stand in four different zones, so a single zone would be false for three of them, and each key resolves its own. Their squares, from the Giver block: Argus Port Bastok (L-7), Cleades Bastok Markets (D-11), Malduc Metalworks (J-8), Rashid Bastok Mines (H-10). I did NOT add a rung for accepting the mission -- the start block is where the giver lives and the walkthrough's lead-in line ('accept it from the Gate Guard') is not a numbered bullet.

RANK GATE, UNMODELLED. The walkthrough's unnumbered lead-in says to trade 3+ Crystals to the Conquest NPC to raise the Rank bar before the mission unlocks. That is a rank-bar requirement and the schema has no field for it; it is emphatically NOT gates.level, which means character level, so gates.level stays null and this goes here with rank_gate_unmodelled.

EXPANSION. The header's Expansion field reads 'bastok', which is a nation code the template picked up, not an expansion. gates.expansion is null rather than an invented value. gates.repeatable is false because the header says 'Repeatable: No' in words.

JUDGEMENT CALLS. (a) Bullets [1] and [2] of the shared walkthrough are one rung on Naji: he escorts you in to President Karst by cutscene rather than you walking to Karst, and the [KI] Letter to the consuls arrives at the end of the interview, so the key item is rung 1's evidence. The bottom option 'No questions.' skips the interview. (b) Baraka is her own rung -- the page tells you to speak to her, then to Helaku 'in the back room', so she is an instruction and not a bystander -- but the page gives her no square, so her grid is null. (c) Helaku's (K-10) is not stated in Option 1; the SAME page states it in Option 2 bullet [8] ('Helaku in Northern San d'Oria (K-10)'), and I used it. That is this record's own page, not a sibling. (d) Bullet [7] is two rungs: examining the Burning Circle and the fight it starts. I put both in Balga's Dais because that is the order the page itself writes ('enter Balga's Dais, and examine the Burning Circle'); a player normally reaches the Dais through that circle from Giddeus, so the zone on rung 9 may be a page infelicity -- rung 9 is medium for that reason. (e) THE BCNM ON THIS ROUTE HAS NO EVIDENCE. The Option 2 section says its battlefield yields the [KI] Kindred crest; the Option 1 section says nothing of the kind for the Black Dragon fight, so I left rung 10's evidence null rather than carry the other branch's outcome across the split. (f) Rung 12 (Naji again) is a real return-to-giver bullet on the page -- Option 1 [9], 'to complete the Mission and advance to Rank 3' -- so it is recorded, not invented. The sub-bullet about Malduc giving the NEXT mission is not a step. (g) The Cipher: Halver / Cipher: Semih, Rhapsodies of Vana'diel and Voracious Resurgence sub-bullets are Trust-system commentary, and the travel routes under both '==' sub-headings are itineraries, not steps.

GROUNDING GATE. check_grounded.py reports start.npc as ungrounded because it matches whole strings and the page never writes the four names joined by ' or ' -- but every one of Argus, Cleades, Malduc and Rashid is on this record's own rendered page, in the '## Giver' block. That is the tool's own first documented hole ('IT MATCHES STRINGS, NOT ENTITIES'), not an imported value. I did not touch the baseline file. | CORRECTED: start.npc is the page's own phrase again. An earlier draft expanded it to the four guards by hand; data/npc_overrides.lua already maps "any bastok gate guard" to exactly those names with zone=false (any zone), so expanding it in the record bypassed a tested mechanism and produced ONE marker key out of the whole sentence -- which matches no entity, so all four guards lost their marker.

  step 6: Back to the Consulate of Bastok; he now orders you on to Windurst, which is the half of this route the other record does first.
  step 10: EVIDENCE DELIBERATELY NULL: the Option 2 section says its battlefield yields the [KI] Kindred crest, but the Option 1 section names no key item for this one, and carrying the other branch's outcome across the split is exactly the import this record must not make.

notes:
THE RENDERED PAGE SAYS THERE IS NO WALKTHROUGH AND THAT IS A RENDERER ARTEFACT, NOT THE TRUTH ABOUT THE PAGE. My rendered .md prints '(the page has no Walkthrough section)', and an earlier machine reading of this mission concluded from that the page 'is an infobox and nothing else' and authored it start-only with zero steps. That is wrong. The cached wikitext at THIS revision (775145, sha 6664869b...) carries a full eleven-bullet walkthrough. It is invisible to stage A only because the page writes its heading as a level-one '=Walkthrough=' while lib/wikitext.py's _HEADING regex requires two or more '=' signs, so section() finds nothing and the prepass prints its placeholder. Everything below is read from that walkthrough -- the same page, the same revision, the same source_sha256 this record is pinned to. Nothing here comes from a sibling page, and check_grounded.py's haystack includes this page's own raw wikitext, which is exactly the text I read.

BULLET NUMBERING IS MINE. The walkthrough's top-level bullets are plain '*' items with no numbers, so I numbered them 1..11 in page order and source_bullets refers to that numbering: [1] Iron Eater, [2] the (G-5) tunnel, [3] the (H-8) door, [4] the (I-10) door, [5] the ??? at the Galka Statue, [6] the Galka Statue again, [7] the (D-12) entrance, [8] the (K-8) doors, [9] the (G-8) weight device, [10] the ??? at the mural, [11] return to Iron Eater. The unnumbered lead-in line about Crystals is cited by no rung.

GIVER. The header's Start is the ROLE 'Any Bastok Gate Guard'. There is no NPC of that name, and normalize_npc discards any string beginning 'Any ' as generic, so copying the header literally costs the mission its marker. The rendered '## Giver' block names all four Bastok gate guards from Category:Gate Guard and any one of them opens the mission, so start.npc is the four-way multi-option string that build_index splits on ' or ' into one marker key each. start.zone and start.grid are null because the four stand in four different zones and each key resolves its own; their squares, from the Giver block, are Argus Port Bastok (L-7), Cleades Bastok Markets (D-11), Malduc Metalworks (J-8) and Rashid Bastok Mines (H-10). This corrects the earlier record, which kept only Argus.

RANK GATE, UNMODELLED. The walkthrough's lead-in requires trading enough Crystals to the Conquest NPC to raise the Rank bar before the mission unlocks. There is no schema field for a rank bar, and it is not gates.level (character level), so gates.level stays null and the requirement is recorded here with rank_gate_unmodelled.

GATES. gates.repeatable is false because the header says 'Repeatable: No' in words. gates.expansion is 'Rise of the Zilart' in the header, written here as the corpus's short code 'rotz'. The header's Level field is empty and no bullet states a level, so gates.level is null -- 'trivial at 99 with Trusts' is advice about difficulty, not a requirement.

THE ORNATE DOORS AND THE LOADSTONE. A red note above the walkthrough says completing the quest Open Sesame lets you pass the weighted Ornate Doors SOLO with the [KI] Loadstone, and that getting through the Quicksand Caves is required to reach the objective. The door bullets themselves state the alternative: three weight points open a door, and a Galka counts 3, a Hume/Elvaan/Mithra 2, a Tarutaru 1 -- so a lone Galka or two of anyone else also opens it. None of that is expressible as an item you hold, so the door rungs carry items [] with items_partial true and the alternatives written out in their notes; Loadstone is not put in items because the doors are passable without it.

JUDGEMENT CALLS. (a) Bullet [5] is two rungs: checking the ??? in front of the Galka Statue, and the three Antica NMs it spawns. 'Clear out the room' comes first in the same bullet and names nothing, so it lives in the examine rung's note rather than becoming a rung with no target and no mobs. (b) Bullet [7] contradicts itself on the square: the bullet says to proceed to (D-12) of Western Altepa Desert while its own sub-bullet says the entrance 'is accessed at (C/D-11) in the far south-west corner'. I recorded (D-12), which is the square the instruction gives, noted the other, and demoted that rung to medium (grid_conflict). (c) Bullet [9] says 'another weight device' and names nothing, so its target is {type: none, name: null} -- by context it is another weighted Ornate Door, but the page does not say so and naming it would be inventing (unnamed_target). (d) (H-8) appears twice, on rung 3 (Map 7) and rung 11 (Map 6); those are different rooms on different maps that share a square label, not a contradiction. (e) The page writes 'Ornate Door' singular in one bullet and 'Ornate Doors' plural in another for the same kind of entity; I used the singular consistently and both forms are on the page. (f) NOTHING IN THIS MISSION IS OBSERVABLE. No bullet grants a key item or an item -- the Loadstone is a precondition you bring, not something this mission gives -- and the header's only Reward is Rank Points, so every rung's evidence is null. That is the honest answer, not a gap. (g) Rung 12 is the page's own 'Return to Iron Eater for a final cutscene' bullet: a real return-to-giver instruction, recorded because it is written, and the page gives Iron Eater no square in either mention so both his rungs have grid null.

steps.note: Walkthrough bullet [1] in my numbering of the page's unnumbered '*' bullets. He is at the President's Office in the Metalworks and the sub-bullet says to keep talking to him until the text stops changing, which is one conversation and one rung. Opening it needs 3 weight points and the sub-bullet gives the table Galka 3, Hume/Elvaan/Mithra 2, Tarutaru 1 or the [KI] Loadstone from the quest Open Sesame, which lets any race do it solo. Loadstone is deliberately NOT in items, because the door is passable without it.

I recorded (D-12) because that is the square the instruction gives, and this rung is medium for it.
